newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends softer but pares losses.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends softer but pares losses.

text.p: COMEX copper settled lower in relatively light trading, recovering some of the losses from a late morning slump as the market failed to follow through on last week's gains.

"We are going to see a continuation of the trading range with maybe an upward bias as demand improves," said David Rinehimer of Smith Barney. It was still questionable if demand is strong enough to keep prices above 90 cents per pound for the December contract, he added.
The market awaited an LME stock drawdown of 5,000 to 7,000 tonnes Tuesday, and this expectation was already factored into the market and helping to keep prices above 90 cents.
December copper settled 1.15 cents weaker at 90.10 cents per pound, traded 91.40 to 89.50 cents. Volume was estimated at 6,500 lots compared to Friday's official 10,121 lots.
The labor contract at Kennecott Copper expires September 30. Company and union officials were unavailable for comment.
Meanwhile a Phelps Dodge official said the union had suggested a late October date to meet regarding a new labor contract at the company's Chino copper mine in New Mexico.
Chino has been operating normally since the previous three year labor deal expired at the end of June.
